title: Container/dependency refresh process + staleness pipeline
context: Container recipes and pinned dependency versions become stale as base images are updated and packages release new versions. Bit-rot — exercises that silently stop building — is rated as a high-likelihood risk in PLAN.md. A documented staleness pipeline converts CI failures to maintenance tasks automatically so the maintainer never has to manually monitor for drift. The process must identify a steward responsible for running periodic refreshes. Depends on: container-ci-005.
objective: Document the container/dependency refresh process and staleness pipeline: how scheduled CI detects upstream base-image drift, how CI failures generate maintenance issues/tasks, how a steward handles the refresh, and what the version-pinning update procedure is.
acceptanceCriteria: Staleness detection process documented: scheduled CI rebuild configuration, what a 'stale' detection looks like (base-image digest mismatch or package-version conflict), and how the CI marks the affected lesson as stale.
Process for converting CI staleness failures to maintenance tasks documented (e.g., CI failure -> auto-creates GitHub issue with a 'stale-lesson' label -> triaged to a maintenance task).

Version-pinning update procedure documented step-by-step: how to update a base-image digest, how to regenerate a conda lockfile, how to verify the updated recipe passes CI before marking the lesson current.
Steward role and responsibilities for the refresh process identified: who owns it, how often periodic reviews are scheduled, and what the escalation path is if a refresh introduces a breaking change.
Document committed to the project repo with DCO sign-off; reviewed and signed off by Maintainer and Technical reviewer.
output: REFRESH-PROCESS.md committed to the project repo documenting the staleness pipeline, version-pinning update procedure, and steward responsibilities; Maintainer and Technical reviewer sign-offs.
